archetype.name: Lottery Team (broken offense, elite glass)
archetype.definition: A team whose rebounding and middling defense can't cover for the league's worst offense, leaving it in the bottom tier and pointed toward a high pick unless its shooting comes back.

report.headline: Last year's top-five offense has collapsed; only the glass is keeping it upright
report.take:
Charlotte arrives at mid-November 4-9 and 24th on the site, and the record flatters it. The margin implies two wins, not four, and the W vs Pt Diff of +2 is the second-luckiest mark in the league. The Net Rtg of -11.3 ranks 28th. This is a sharp turn from a year ago, when the Hornets went 44-38 with a +5.0 Net Rtg, a fifth-ranked offense and a 119.4 ORtg. Last season was itself an outlier against three straight losing years, so the open question is which version is the real one.

The offense is the whole story. The ORtg of 103.8 is dead last, more than ten points under the league. Charlotte still takes the league's highest share of its shots from three (51.5% 3PA Rate), but it is making only 31.3% of them, down from 37.8% last year. It also gets to the line less than anyone (21.6 FT Rate) and turns it over more than anyone (16.9 TOV %, against 13.5 last year). That is the worst profile possible for a three-heavy team: low-percentage shots, no free points, and empty trips. The burden falls on Brandon Miller (32.2 USG %, 45.3 TS %) and Naz Reid (28.9 USG %, 48.4 TS %), who use the most possessions and convert them poorly. Grayson Allen is scoring with real efficiency (67.8 TS %) on far less usage. The backcourt grade is an F, and Dennis Schröder (BPM -7.9) is out.

The numbers hide two things that should help. First, the Hornets lead the league in ORB %, DRB % and REB %, a real, repeatable edge built on a center rotation that controls the paint. Opponents' centers have produced less against Charlotte than against almost anyone. Second, the defense is closer to average than the record suggests: a 115.1 DRtg (16th) and an 8th-ranked Opp Rim FG %. The big leak is opponents hitting 40.5% from three, the worst mark in the league. Some of that is shooters' luck that should cool. The same logic applies to Charlotte's own 3P %, which is unlikely to stay this far below last year's.

So the underlying team is better than a -11.3 but nowhere near last year's +5.0. November has been worse than October on defense, and the lineup data says the best minutes come with Ryan Kalkbrenner (+20.9 On-Off) rather than Reid (-8.2) or Moussa Diabaté (-15). Shooting regression should lift the offense off the floor. The turnovers and the lack of free throws are structural, and they cap the ceiling. Expect a team that plays closer games but still lives in the lottery.

strengths.title: League's best rebounding team, both ends
strengths.body: Charlotte ranks first in ORB %, DRB % and REB %, comfortably above the league averages. This is a frontcourt story: Reid and Diabaté each have over 100 rebounds, and opposing centers rank first-fewest in rebounds against them. Effort-and-size edges like this tend to hold, and they give a poor-shooting team its extra possessions.

strengths.title: Interior defense holds up
strengths.body: Opponents shoot only 62.7% at the rim (8th), and the overall DRtg sits 16th, near league average. Centers have been neutralized, ranking 3rd-fewest in points allowed to the position. The defense is not the problem; it is being dragged down by the three-point line.

strengths.title: Kalkbrenner and Allen work
strengths.body: Ryan Kalkbrenner posts a 71.6 TS % in a low-usage role, and the team is +20.9 per 100 better with him on the floor. Grayson Allen is the one efficient perimeter scorer, at 67.8 TS %. Both point to lineups that could be steadier if they got more of the minutes.

concerns.title: Worst offense in the league
concerns.body: The 103.8 ORtg ranks 30th, down from 119.4 a year ago. Every shooting measure is bottom-three: eFG %, TS % and 3P %. Charlotte keeps launching threes at a league-high rate while making 31.3% of them, against 37.8% last season. Some bounce-back is likely, but the shot diet magnifies every cold night.

concerns.title: Turnovers and no free throws
concerns.body: A 30th-ranked TOV % of 16.9 and a 30th-ranked FT Rate of 21.6 mean the offense wastes possessions and never gets easy points. Neither problem is about shooting luck, so neither should be expected to fix itself. These two numbers, more than the cold threes, are what separate this team from last year's.

concerns.title: High-usage stars, low efficiency
concerns.body: Miller uses 32.2% of possessions at a 45.3 TS %, and Reid 28.9% at 48.4. The team is worse with Reid on the floor (-8.2 On-Off). Until the primary options convert, the offense has no floor, and the F backcourt grade with Schröder out leaves little organizing help.

trend.note: A 3-4 October gave way to a 1-5 November, with the defense slipping from 106.43 to 113.83 points allowed a game while scoring stayed near 100. The last five games show slightly better scoring, but the record (1-4) has not followed.

weekAhead.headline: Two road games against winners, then red-hot Memphis
weekAhead.body:
All three opponents have winning records and rank in the site's top 14. The Lakers are third with the league's best offense, and Memphis is seventh with a top-ten offense and defense. Charlotte's rebounding edge is its one reliable lever. The Lakers rank 29th in DRB %, which sets up second-chance points. The trouble is that both the Lakers and Hawks rank top-three at forcing turnovers, the exact weakness the Hornets carry.

The Atlanta game is the most winnable. The Hawks' rim defense is soft (69.1% Opp Rim FG %, 26th), and they give up heavy production to centers, which suits a frontcourt-centric attack. Memphis, by contrast, shoots 39.2% from three against a defense that has allowed opponents 40.5%. A one-win week would be par; a sweep of losses would not be a surprise.

keyMatchups.title: Hornets glass vs Lakers' DRB %
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte leads the league in ORB %, while Los Angeles ranks 29th in DRB %. Extra possessions are the only way a 30th-ranked offense keeps pace with a 123.0 ORtg. If the Hornets also give the ball away against a top-three turnover-forcing defense, the edge disappears.

keyMatchups.title: Centers attack Atlanta's paint
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows 23.29 points a game to centers (28th) and a 69.1% Opp Rim FG %. That is the best opening of the week for Reid, Diabaté and Kalkbrenner. Pounding the rim also beats settling for threes against a Hawks defense that is decent on the perimeter.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis shooters vs leaky arc
keyMatchups.body: The Grizzlies make 39.2% of their threes (2nd), and Charlotte allows the league's highest Opp 3P % at 40.5. Memphis also defends shooting guards well, which squeezes Allen, Charlotte's most efficient scorer. This is the matchup most likely to get away early.

weekAhead.watch: Charlotte's turnover count against the Lakers' and Hawks' pressure; if the Hornets keep it near their season norm, the rebounding edge has a chance to matter.

restOfSeason.body:
Some of this collapse should reverse. A team that shot 37.8% from three last year is unlikely to stay at 31.3%, and opponents probably won't keep hitting 40.5% against a defense that protects the rim well. Both should pull the -11.3 Net Rtg toward the middle-negative range. Working the other way, the +2 W vs Pt Diff will likely give back wins, and the turnover and free-throw problems look like features of this roster rather than noise. The site's 82-game pace of 25 wins is a fair midpoint.

The realistic upside is a team that plays roughly .400 ball the rest of the way once the shooting normalizes. That lands somewhere in the high 20s, well short of last year's 44 and outside play-in range in most seasons. The downside is the current trajectory continuing if Miller and Reid keep using a third of the possessions inefficiently.
swingFactors: Whether Miller's and Reid's shooting efficiency recovers
How much opponents' 40.5% from three cools off

confidence.note: Only 13 games, but the turnover, free-throw and rebounding profiles are consistent across both months.
